objective:
Second-pass indicator tuning for a trader who is REQUIRED to trade BTC and ETH perps at exactly 100x leverage on Papertrade (papertrade.xyz) and wants the best achievable settings and setups, even if no setup shows a proven positive edge.

Attached inputs (read them first): the first tuning pass report (tuningReport) and its machine-readable results (tuning), which found that none of ten indicators (Bollinger, moving averages, MA ribbon, SuperTrend, Ichimoku, TD Sequential, RSI, MACD, Stochastic, Volume) had positive out-of-sample net expectancy at 100x (best: TD Sequential -0.020 R over 59 trades, RSI -0.035 R over 1,079), and the Papertrade mechanics research (papertradeResearch) that defines the payout math, fees, asymmetric impact and bust rules. Public links: https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/9192786bee06cc298914a72245224d5c1a6445d025c51db37a89f3de12e6da7a , https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/f1c8591e30a2e8945ec176d7a162156e4ac4737aff45749110a99828fa401d11 , https://api.imd.fun/artifacts/6e8652275deb7261fcc223d0cbcb13342ab70f0f84d1a3063dff85857a9af858 .

Goal: given leverage is fixed at 100x, find for EACH of the ten indicators the best-case configuration, and the overall best playbook. Go well beyond a plain parameter sweep:
- Fresh, longer data: fetch at least 120 days of public 1m BTC and ETH perp candles (Hyperliquid candleSnapshot if reachable, else OKX BTC-USDT-SWAP/ETH-USDT-SWAP history-candles or Binance USDT-M klines) and build 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m and 1h bars.
- Exit design matters more than entry at 100x: test stop placement inside the bust distance (as a fraction of the bust distance), asymmetric targets that compensate Papertrade's discount on profitable moves, partial take-profits, break-even moves, trailing exits and short time stops.
- Filters: trend regime (higher-timeframe EMA slope or ADX), volatility regime (ATR percentile; skip when the expected adverse excursion exceeds the stop), session and hour-of-day, day-of-week, BTC/ETH cross-confirmation, and multi-timeframe confluence.
- Combinations: test pairs and triples of indicators where one sets direction and another times entry (for example a trend filter plus an oscillator trigger), and selectivity (fewer, higher-quality trades).
- Robustness: walk-forward with at least three rolling folds, parameter-stability heatmaps or neighbourhood checks (prefer plateaus over spikes), a cost and slippage sensitivity sweep, and a deflated or multiple-testing-aware view of the best result. Report out-of-sample numbers as the headline and flag any result that depends on a narrow parameter spike or a small sample.
- Objective: rank by out-of-sample mean net R per trade with a minimum trade count, and separately by lowest bust rate and smallest drawdown, because a forced 100x trader also needs to survive. Pick the single best-case setting for each indicator even if its expectancy is still negative, and say how negative.

For each indicator deliver exact, unambiguous long and short rules: timeframe, parameters, trigger, which bar confirms, entry price assumption, stop (percent of price and fraction of bust distance), target and trailing rules, time stop, filters, and do-not-trade conditions; plus out-of-sample trades, win rate, mean R, profit factor, max drawdown, bust rate and the fold-by-fold results. Then give a recommended 100x playbook: the best one to three setups, daily loss limit and trade frequency, margin per trade as a share of account, and what would make the trader stop. State plainly whether anything shows a positive edge and how confident that is.
